transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because... well, I lost my temper on a board call recently. Someone asked a small question about the facility budget, and I just snapped at them. That’s not how I run my company. It’s not how I treat people, and it’s not like me at all. I figured I needed to talk to someone about it.
Did something stressful happen in your life recently before this started?
Yeah, there was. All of this... well, it's been going on for about six days now. It started right after we had an explosion and a fire during a walkthrough at one of the sites.
Since the explosion and fire, have you felt emotionally upset because of what happened?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I'm emotionally upset. I mean... I haven't been feeling sad or down or anything like that. It's just, well, like I said, I've been snapping at people. But I'm not sitting around crying about what happened, if that's what you mean.
Since this started, have you been needing much less sleep than usual?
No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I'm still sleeping about the same amount I usually do. I wouldn't say I need less of it.
Since this started, have you been feeling unusually upbeat or euphoric?

No, definitely not. I haven't felt upbeat or... euphoric, or anything like that. There's really nothing to be upbeat about right now anyway. I just feel normal, aside from being short with people like I said.
Since the explosion, have you been feeling unusually nervous or on edge?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel nervous... or on edge. I'm not walking around feeling anxious or jumping at shadows or anything like that. I'm just going about my business, really, except for being a little quick to snap at folks like I mentioned.
Since the explosion, have you been feeling down or depressed?

No, I haven't felt depressed. I'm not really the type to get down in the dumps anyway. I'm just going to work and handling things like normal... well, except for the snapping at people part. But no, I don't feel sad or depressed at all.
Since the explosion, have unwanted memories of it been popping into your mind?

Yeah, they actually have. I'll just be right in the middle of a phone call, or sitting there looking at some numbers for the business, and it just happens. The blast, and seeing that fire over by the loading area... they just jump right back into my head out of nowhere. It's honestly like a bad film I didn't ask to see. It just pops up while I'm trying to work.
Since the explosion, have you had moments when it felt like you were reliving it, as if it were happening again?

No, I wouldn't say that. It's just the memories popping into my head, like I said. I know I'm sitting at my desk when it happens, I don't feel like I'm actually back there at the warehouse when it blew. It's just a memory, not like it's happening all over again right in front of me.
Since the explosion, have you been avoiding places or situations that remind you of it?

Yeah, I suppose I have. I've been keeping away from the new building entirely. And, well, even the mortgage folder and the safety reports for it... they're just sitting on my desk unopened. Every time I go to reach for them, my stomach just drops, so I leave them be.
Since the explosion, have there been times when you felt numb, dazed, or like things around you weren’t quite real?

Yeah, actually. Sometimes when I'm taking calls from the house... the room just starts looking sort of distant. And my own voice, it sounds strange to me. It's almost like... well, like I'm watching myself talk instead of being fully there in the room. It's a weird feeling.
Since the explosion, has this been interfering with your work or your ability to handle things day to day?

Yeah, I'd say it is. I mean, I'm still technically working, but... I'm delaying decisions about the facility. I'm leaning on other people to handle calls that I would normally just take myself. And, well, my reaction on a recent board call kind of made me realize that this is actually starting to affect my judgment and my leadership.
